correctness.rationale: Every unit is a diagonal tuple of nonzero scalars plus an arbitrary arrow tuple. Equality gh=hg reduces to (d_s-d_t)y=(b_s-b_t)x on each arrow. For monochromatic-edge flat H and nonzero support S within H, the centralizer has exactly q^{|H|}(q-1)^{n-r(S)} elements; orbit-stabilizer gives q^{m-|H|}(q-1)^{r(S)}. Counting x of fixed support then dividing by orbit size gives (q-1)^{|S|-r(S)} classes per vertex coloring. The number of colorings whose exact equality-edge set is H is (q-1)^c chi_{M/H}(q-1), yielding every coefficient of equation (1). Independently Burnside and the monochromatic-edge expansion give (q-1)^c T_M(q,q). Loops and parallel arrows satisfy the same identities, including characteristic two; 14 exhaustive small literal group calculations checked q=2,3,4. Finite tests are not the general proof.

value.rationale: The group-theoretic conjugacy class sizes form an intrinsic natural invariant of each finite algebra unit group. Equation (1) gives every multiplicity, uniformly in arbitrary quiver size/loops/parallel edges/all finite fields; (2) identifies an unexpected graphic-matroid Tutte-diagonal evaluation and explains orientation invariance and forest counts. The all-parameter classification and structural bridge to graphic matroids are mathematically motivated, not a narrow recomputation, and the size-resolved result is not implied by previously known specialized total counts.
